 LIVE UPDATES NBA Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Philadelphia 76ers Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
 Dan Favale Oct 22, 2026, updated 4 min ago 
 After picking up an open-night victory over the reigning-champion New York Knicks, the Philadelphia 76ers are putting their perfect record on the line against the Cleveland Cavaliers Thursday night.
 This matchup will mark the regular-season home debuts for both LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. It is also Peyton Watson's first official game with the Cavs, as well as Cleveland's first overall tilt of the 2026-27 campaign.
 Follow along below for updates, highlights, analysis and takeaways from this showdown between should-be Eastern Conference superpowers.
 Live Updates
 38 Total Posts
 Newest First ​ Just Now 08:45 PM The Cavs are in Danger of Making the WRONG Kind of History
 Find a team that loves blowing 20-plus point leads in the second half as much as the Cleveland Cavaliers of past six months. I dare you.
 Score: Sixers 106, Cavs 100 | 2:11 remaining in the fourth quarter 
 11 mins ago 08:38 PM Welcome Home, Jaylen Brown
 Jaylen Brown has two buckets in the fourth. They've both been absolutely monstrous. 
 Things are getting chippy on the floor. The crowd is unreal. This feels like a playoff game. Which come to think of it, explains James Harden's offensive performance.
 14 mins ago 08:34 PM Tyrese Maxey and James Harden are Getting into It
 Friendship is overrated, apparently.
 Or it's just hard to maintain while immersed in the throes of a 36-point turnaround-slash-implosion.
 Score: Sixers 102, Cavs 95 | 4:58 remaining in the fourth quarter 
 17 mins ago 08:31 PM The Shot that Completed the Sixers' Turnaround
 Following a Jaylen Brown step-back jumper, the Sixers are now actually up three. That's a 32-point turnaround. Which is insane.
 Score: Sixers 98, Cavs 85 | 5:36 remaining in the fourth quarter 
 19 mins ago 08:29 PM The Cavs' Lead has VANISHED
 What a comeback from Philly.
 And what a potential meltdown from Cleveland. 
 22 mins ago 08:27 PM The Greatest Mid-Game Player Interview of All Time?
 These mid-game player interviews generally don't yield much. We could all probably do without them. 
 Except this one. Maxey explaining the importance of Game 2-of-82 resilience has me ready to run through a brick wall, and if need be, follow him into hell.
 24 mins ago 08:25 PM Mario Hezonja for Comeback Player of the Year?
 Mario Hezonja is giving the Cavs great minutes off the bench. He has more points (10) than James Harden (9) and is playing with a coordinated physicality he didn't have during his first go-round at the NBA level.
 While the NBA doesn't have an official Comeback Player of the Year honor, Hezonja is the odds-on favorite to take it home in spirit. Especially following the Ben Simmons Achilles injury.
 Score: Cavs 95, Sixers 89 | 8:24 remaining in the fourth quarter 
 31 mins ago 08:17 PM This Sixers Defensive Shift May Have Changed the Game 
 Philly is opening up the fourth using the same approach. LeBron is guarding Evan Mobley, and Joel Embiid continues to roam, mostly off of Mario Hezonja.
 34 mins ago 08:14 PM We're Heading for a Wild Finish in Philly
 The Sixers outscored the Cavaliers 37-21 in the third quarter to cut their deficit to eight points. Their play was a complete 180. 
 LeBron James hit another gear on offense. Tyrese Maxey was a human blur at both ends. The defense was sensational.
 Donovan Mitchell's shot-making have helped Cleveland stem the tide. Mario Hezonja (yes, him) also hit two big buckets to close the third. 
 Grab your popcorn. It looks like we're heading for a photo finish.
 Score: Cavs 90, Sixers 82 | End of the third quarter 
 42 mins ago 08:07 PM LeBron Gave VJ a Bloody Nose 😳
 Seriously, how can you not love VJ Edgecombe? He's doing all the dirty work for the Sixers—defending, running, cutting, passing, even rebounding. His job description apparently includes taking elbows from LeBron, too.
 For anyone wondering, the elbow was not on purpose. Philly's two stars were going after a rebound off a missed free throw.
 Score: Cavs 84, Sixers 80 | 2:45 remaining in the third quarter 
 48 mins ago 08:01 PM Cleveland's Lead is Almost Gone
 Kofie might be on to something here.
 Score: Cavs 80, Sixers 75 | 3:59 remaining in the third quarter 
 52 mins ago 07:57 PM Tyrese Maxey is Terrorizing the Cavs
 I'm not sure where Tyrese Maxey landed on all the preseason rankings floating around the interwebz. But I'm certain it was too low.
 He's now up to 21 points, five assists and two steals. And he's getting "M-V-P" chants from the crowd as I type this.
 55 mins ago 07:53 PM This Jaylen Brown Finish is TOUGH
 Difficulty level: 11/10. 
 Philly already has eight made buckets at the hoop in the third, driven largely by forcing turnovers and starting to run more often. A Tyrese Maxey transition three just cut the lead to seven .
 Score: Cavs 80, Sixers 73 | 5:18 remaining in the third quarter 
 59 mins ago 07:49 PM The Sixers' Comeback is on
 Everything has tightened up for the Sixers. The defense. The ball control. The shot selection. They're dominating the third quarter. 
 The comeback is being fueled by an emphasis on getting into the paint. This is one of a couple finishes on the break from LeBron. Jaylen Brown has two finishes at the hoop himself. Joel Embiid has gotten closer to the basket as well.
 Also, Tyrese Maxey just keeps coming up with steals.
 Score: Cavs 79, Sixers 66 | 6:58 remaining in the third quarter 
 1 hour ago 07:38 PM The Cavs Defense is Thriving at LeBron's Expense
 Mind you, it's not just LeBron. The Sixers as a team have eight turnovers on 12 transition plays, according to Prime Stats . 
 On the bright side, they're taking better care of the ball to start the third quarter. They have come out of the locker room to score eight straight points. The crowd is back into it as well. 
 Score: Cavs 69, Sixers 53 | 11:09 remaining in the third quarter 
 1 hour ago 07:24 PM The Cavs Take a 24-Point Lead into Halftime
 Jarrett Allen is balling right alongside Donovan Mitchell and Evan Mobley, too. He takes 14 points and five boards into the locker room. 
 Cleveland building a 24-point lead while having a relatively quiet night from James Harden (six points, three assists) doesn't bode well for the Sixers. Tyrese Maxey (15 points, two assists) is the only player making this watchable from Philly's end.
 Jaylen Brown is a ghost right now. He has almost as many turnovers (three) as points (four). LeBron James is turnover machine at the moment as well. He's responsible for five of the Sixers' 14 giveaways. The dedication to featuring Joel Embiid is starting to feel like a version of self-destruction.
 Score: Cavs 69, Sixers 45 | HALFTIME 
 1 hour ago 07:17 PM Nothing is Coming Easy for the Sixers
 Is scoring 0.45 points per transition possession bad? 
 (Yes, it's putrid.)
 1 hour ago 07:10 PM LeBron's First Dunk at Home
 Kudos to Sixers fans for getting loud on this one. They so badly want something to cheer right now.
 Maybe, just maybe, the Sixers can give it to them. 
 And yet, as I type this, Philly committed a turnover and the crowed started booing. Can't say I blame them.
 Score: Cavs 62, Sixers 35 | 2:48 remaining in the second quarter 
 1 hour ago 07:05 PM Incredible View of LeBron's Chalk Toss 
 This photo is the best thing the Sixers have going for them in the first half.
 1 hour ago 07:03 PM Numbers Don't Lie...
 ...even if the Sixers wish they did.
 This is quickly becoming a butt-kicking. Richard Jefferson is already asking "What's the record for turnovers?" on the ESPN broadcast.
 Score: Cavs 54, Sixers 30 | 5:42 remaining in the second quarter 
 1 hour ago 07:01 PM Evan Mobley is Going Kaboom
 Evan Mobley is already up to 11 second-quarter points while doing a bit of everything. Not only did he bury this pull-up out of an inverted pick-and-roll, but he just nailed a wing three—a shot that's always going to be there for him.
 Apart from Tyrese Maxey, the Sixers don't have much going for them. They have turned the ball over on more than 30 percent of their possessions for the game and can't seem to grab a rebound in the second quarter.
 Score: Cavs 52, Sixers 28 | 6:43 remaining in the second quarter 
 1 hour ago 06:53 PM Kenny Atkinson is Experimenting with Cleveland's Lineups
 Rolling with the Donovan Mitchell-Evan Mobley pairing makes sense in a vacuum. Jarrett Allen is the prototypical James Harden big man.
 Still, Mobley and Harden were actually one of Cleveland's better pick-and-roll duos by the end of last season. Going away from that may be a vote of confidence in Mobley's creation independent of Harden. Or just proof that the Cavs won't stick to any hard-and-fast staggering patterns.
 At any rate, Cleveland has opened up a 20-point lead and is threatening to expand it even further.
 Score: Cavs 44, Sixers 24 | 9:12 remaining in the second quarter 
 1 hour ago 06:49 PM Spida with the Sick First-Quarter Dagger 🗡️
 Donovan Mitchell is locked in at both ends right now. On top of this first-quarter buzzer-beater, he is 5-of-5 at the charity stripe and has come up with a few big defensive plays.
 2 hours ago 06:47 PM It's All Cavs Through the First Quarter
 Philly's offense is a brutal watch right now. Not enough ball movement. Too many one-on-one possessions. Even more turnovers. Just 2-of-8 shooting from downtown. 
 The list goes on.
 Cleveland's defense deserves a lot of credit for not overcommitting to any of Philly's ball-handlers. Donovan Mitchell has been active, bagging two steals and one block. The Cavs are running the floor nicely, too. They already have an 8-0 lead in transition.
 Score: Cavs 35, Sixers 18 | End of the first quarter 
 2 hours ago 06:42 PM Sweet LeBron ➡️ VJ Dime
 Remember when people were worried about VJ Edgecombe figuring out how to score on this team?
 Yeah, I don't, either. 
 Not every 21-year-old drafted in the top five barely a year ago is hard-wired to run and cut his way to baskets on an endless loop. Edgecombe seems different.
 In other news: The Cavs have fleshed out a 14-point lead.
 Score: Cavs 32, Sixers 18 | 24.6 seconds remaining in the first quarter 
 2 hours ago 06:37 PM LeBron and Embiid Already Have a Special Handshake 🤝
 We interrupt your on-court updates with an important observation: NBA players are exceptionally talented at developing special handshakes with new teammates.
 Not surprisingly, LeBron might just be the very best of all time at it.
 2 hours ago 06:34 PM Peyton Watson is Already Block 3s for Cleveland
 It's fair to say (a healthy) Max Strus wasn't going to do this .
 Getting around even a half-baked Joel Embiid screen is no small task. Watson just made it look easy.
 Cleveland opened a double-digit lead just a bit later. Philly's offense lacks flow and is heavy on Embiid one-on-one possessions. The threes aren't falling, either. Head coach Nick Nurse has since turned to his Tyrese Maxey-Jaylen Brown-plus-the-bench lineup to bridge the gap.
 Score: Cavs 25, Sixers 16 | 2:00 remaining in the first quarter 
 2 hours ago 06:26 PM LeBron's First Home Bucket in Philly
 The crowd reaction, again, stands out here. As does the fact LeBron's first bucket was a three rather than a trademark finishing off a drive.
 This is one of the few Sixers highlights we have so far. They have committed six turnovers out of the gate, three of which have come at LeBron's hands. They're down only two, though.
 Score: Cavs 13, Sixers 11 | 6:18 remaining in the first quarter 
 2 hours ago 06:23 PM Listen to All of Philly React to LeBron's First Intro
 Full stop, I don't think Lakers or Heat fans were this loud for LeBron's first home intro. The Sixers' faithful don't mess around.
 2 hours ago 06:19 PM LeBron's First Chalk Toss in Philly
 Someday, Sixers fans won't react to LeBron's chalk toss like they've just seen a deity. 
 That day is not today.
 2 hours ago 06:18 PM It's a Playoff Atmosphere in Philly
 It's almost like LeBron James and Jaylen Brown are making their regular-season home debuts or something.
 By the way: We're off! LeBron has already hit a three, and the crowd went wild. We also already had LeBron hit VJ Edgecombe on a cut to the hoop. 
 Score: Cavs 6, Sixers 5 | 9:30 remaining in the first quarter 
 2 hours ago 06:14 PM LeBron Can Still Dunk
 Just do the dunk contest already, LeBron. Please. 
 2 hours ago 06:12 PM Jaylen Brown is Ready for his Sixers Home Debut
 And also proof that the rhythm is going to get you.
 2 hours ago 06:11 PM The Real AI is in Building
 No, not Claude. Allen Iverson!
 Did anyone else have Boyz II Men's Christmas Interpretations on cassette growing up? Or was that just me? 
 2 hours ago 05:58 PM 1 Big Question for Peyton Watson
 How much time to the Cavs carve out on-ball for him? 
 Watson ran a lot of the Denver Nuggets' offseason for a beat last year while Nikola Jokić was sidelined. And the Cavs have a need for creation outside of James Harden and Donovan Mitchell. 
 Whether Watson's good enough to provide it is one thing. How the Cavs go about using him offensively when they also have Evan Mobley to account for is another.
 3 hours ago 05:38 PM The Sixers' Frontcourt Injuries Just Keep Coming
 Dean Wade already missed the Sixers' season-opener with this same ankle injury. He is listed as day-to-day, so this doesn't profile as a long-term concern.
 Immediately, though, we should expect to see more units with Jabari Walker—including lineups that feature him or LeBron James at the 5.
 3 hours ago 05:36 PM It's the Usual Starting 5 for Philly
 This group was a plus-eight in 16 minutes against the New York Knicks on Tuesday night. Somewhat surprisingly, they cut their teeth on the defensive end, limiting the reigning champs to just 0.71 points per possession .
 Shooting progression is the big thing to watch. Philly's Fantastic Five(?) hit just two of their 13 three-point attempts to open the season. Something tells me they'll want to convert more than 15.4 percent of their triples moving forward.
 3 hours ago 05:31 PM The Cavs Have Locked in Their Starters
 This is the starting lineup everyone would have predicted. It also makes a ton of sense on paper. 
 Still, it'll be interesting to see how head coach Kenny Atkinson staggers these guys. Part of Peyton Watson's appeal is he might have more skill to explore on-ball. And we'll definitely be seeing one-big units peppered throughout the game.
